title: Rev-Dep Duplicated Code JSON Output
description: JSON output format for rev-dep duplicated-code --format json. Every object sets additionalProperties:false, so a key the tool emits but this file does not declare makes real output fail validation - which is what keeps the two from drifting apart.

version.description: Shape of this document. Bumped whenever a key is added, removed, renamed or changes meaning, so a consumer can tell a tool upgrade from a format change.

tool.description: The command that produced this report

cwd.description: Absolute directory that was analysed. Every path below is relative to it.

snapshot.description: Present only when the run was compared against a baseline

findings.description: Every duplicated pattern the run reported. NOT filtered to what changed when a snapshot is used - filter on the status field for that.

settings.description: Everything that decided which findings are here, so two runs reporting different numbers can be told apart by configuration rather than by guesswork.

blinding.description: Derived label for the three flags below: "exact", "identifiers", "identifiers+strings" and so on

blindIdentifiers.description: Names were wildcards, so renamed copies still matched

blindStrings.description: String and template contents were wildcards

minDepth.description: Smallest reported duplication, in nesting levels counting the block itself

minStatements.description: Smallest reported statement block, in statements. Does not apply to object literals or JSX.

minDuplicates.description: How many copies a chunk needed before it was reported

skipObjects.description: Duplications that are only object literals were dropped

ignoreFiles.description: Glob patterns excluded from the analysis, relative to cwd

processIgnoredFiles.description: Glob patterns analysed despite gitignore, relative to cwd

configLevel.description: Present only when a config file applied its own file selection on top of the above

A config file's top-level file selection. Its patterns are relative to the config rather than to cwd, which is why they are reported separately instead of merged into the lists above - the same string means different files read from the two places.

configPath.description: The config file whose directory the patterns below are resolved against

snapshot.description: The comparison against a committed baseline.

path.description: The snapshot file this run was compared against

clean.description: Whether the run matches the baseline exactly. False for improvements too: a snapshot that overstates duplication is one nobody can trust.

resolved.description: Acknowledged patterns that are gone. Not findings, because there is no code left to report - no occurrences, no metrics, no snippet.

belowThreshold.description: Acknowledged patterns still duplicated, but by fewer copies than minDuplicates requires. They have real code and locations, which is what separates them from resolved ones - and why they are reported at all.

deltaCounts.description: The delta by kind. The names match the status field on findings.

new.description: Not in the snapshot at all

moved.description: Same number of copies, different files

belowThreshold.description: Still duplicated, but below minDuplicates and so no longer reported

snapshotEntry.description: An acknowledged duplication the run has no code for. All that survives is what the snapshot itself recorded.

hash.description: Canonical-form digest: the identity that survives reformatting, plus whatever else the run's blinding ignores

occurrences.description: How many copies were acknowledged. Equals the sum of files.

files.description: Each path mapped to how many copies lived in it

label.description: First line of one occurrence, for a human reading a diff. Takes no part in identity.

summary.description: Aggregates over findings, including the composition that says which kind of block they actually are.

finding.description: One duplicated pattern and every place it appears.

hash.description: Canonical-form digest. Comparable only across runs with the same blinding.

role.description: What a code block's braces actually are

statements.description: Meaningful only for statement blocks; expressions report 0

canonicalChars.description: Size of the canonical form. Informational.

snippet.description: The first occurrence verbatim. Emitted only with --json-snippets.

status.description: How this finding relates to the snapshot. Absent when the run had no snapshot. Filtering on it is how a consumer gets the delta.

was.description: The acknowledged state, for a status that is not unchanged or new

fileChanges.description: Every file whose number of copies moved, so a copy added to a file already on the list is visible rather than folded into the total

was.description: The state a finding was acknowledged in.

fileChange.description: One file whose number of copies moved. was 0 means the file is new to this pattern; now 0 means it holds none of them any more.

occurrence.description: One copy. Byte offsets are exact; line and column are 1-based and inclusive at both ends, which is what makes a range comparable with a tool that reports clones as line spans.
